findings.title: Firestore orders collection is world-readable and writable
findings.attacker: Anyone on the internet. The Firebase project ID ships inside the APK (google-services.json), no login needed.
trace: firestore.rules:5 grants `allow read, write: if true` on /orders/{orderId}
lib/data/order_repository.dart:22 stores customer name, phone and delivery address in /orders
The Firestore REST API accepts unauthenticated requests for this path, so every order can be listed, edited or deleted
findings.impact: Full disclosure of customer PII (names, phone numbers, addresses) and the ability to alter or delete any order.
findings.fix: Require auth and ownership: `allow read, update: if request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId;` and restrict create to the signed-in user's own uid. Deploy with `firebase deploy --only firestore:rules`.
findings.verified_by: verifier-2 (fresh context, re-read rules file and repository code)

findings.title: Promo deep link may load an attacker URL into a WebView with a JS bridge
findings.unresolved: Whether the router validates the `url` query parameter of shop://promo before PromoPage receives it; the GoRouter redirect lives in a private package that was not available to the audit.

findings.title: Google API key in lib/firebase_options.dart
findings.rejection_reason: Firebase client config key. It identifies the project and is public by design; access is governed by Security Rules and App Check, which are covered by F-1.
